title: Socratic Prompt Scheduler & Backoff — personal notebook
content:
Purpose
----
Quick personal sketch for a lightweight prompt scheduling layer that sits between clients and the inference runtime. Focus: improve tail latency and graceful degradation when device-level or tenant-level load spikes happen. Name is silly (Socratic) because it tries to ask the client a small set of probing questions to decide scheduling/backoff behavior.

Problem statement
----
- Clients submit prompts with varying criticality: interactive chat vs background summarization vs embeddings update.
- We need to: prioritize interactive low-token prompts, prefetch likely follow-ups, and apply tenant-aware backoffs that avoid cascading failures.
- Runtime can do batching and KV-cache warm starts; scheduler should be aware of those opportunities.

Goals / requirements
----
1) Minimal change to client SDKs: opt-in headers and small API additions.
2) Server-side scheduler must be able to: 
   - classify requests into priority lanes
   - probe client latency tolerance (socratic probes)
   - run adaptive backoff + retry policies per-tenant or per-route
   - expose observability (queue depth, dropped count, effective latency)
3) Allow per-deployment config: hosted, dedicated, private must be configurable.

Runtime constraints / heuristics
----
- Token-slicing: if a request asks for N tokens and latency budget is tight, consider returning in chunks (streaming) or ask the model to chunk output (system message) — prefer SDK streaming.
- Prefetch+kv-warm: if a user issues a follow-up hint in metadata (probable_next_prompts: true), pre-warm KV cache on warm candidates.
- Backoff tiers: soft (delay 100-500ms), hard (reject with 429 + retry-after), degraded (route to cheaper model variant).

Proposed client API additions (examples)
----
- New optional fields under request metadata: priority, criticality_hint, followup_hint, latency_budget_ms

Example HTTP request body (JSON):
{
  "input": "Summarize the following: ...",
  "metadata": {
    "priority": "interactive",
    "criticality_hint": "user-facing",
    "followup_hint": "likely_short",
    "latency_budget_ms": 300
  }
}

Server response when scheduled immediately:
- normal streaming response with x-scheduler-lane: interactive

Server response when deferred / soft-backoff:
HTTP 202 Accepted
{
  "status": "queued",
  "ticket_id": "s5f-20260101-...",
  "estimated_wait_ms": 220
}

Schema for scheduling config (text/YAML-like inside doc)
----
scheduler:
  default_lane: normal
  lanes:
    - name: interactive
      weight: 0.7
      max_queue_ms: 150
      prefetch: true
      fallback_model: gptx-mini
    - name: batch
      weight: 0.2
      max_queue_ms: 2000
      prefetch: false
      fallback_model: gptx-quant
    - name: background
      weight: 0.1
      max_queue_ms: 10000
      prefetch: false
      fallback_model: none
  backoff:
    soft: { delay_base_ms: 100, jitter: 0.2 }
    hard: { reject_after_ms: 3000, reject_code: 429 }
  tenant_overrides: []

Notes on tenant overrides: allow operators to set per-tenant desired latency SLOs and model fallbacks. E.g., tenant A: interactive lane max_queue_ms=80; tenant B: allow degraded model fallback only at high load.

Socratic probes (lightweight probing handshake)
----
Idea: when a new client session is seen, scheduler sends a short probe in-band that asks the client to provide minimal hints (or the SDK returns them automatically). Probes are cheap 1-2 token metadata exchanges and let scheduler learn: typical prompt length, followup probability, user patience (latency_budget_ms). If SDK can collect past session stats, attach them so probes are skipped.

ASCII diagram (logical)
----
Client SDK --> Ingress Gateway --> Scheduler --> Router --> Runtime (Model Pool)
                         |                        ^
                         |                        |
                         +--> Metrics/Observability <--+

Scheduler lanes: [interactive] [batch] [background]
- Router uses lane + runtime load + available KV cache to pick target host.

Backoff flow samples
----
Case: sudden spike, interactive queue depth high
1) New interactive request arrives with latency_budget 250ms
2) Scheduler checks queue, estimate wait 400ms -> > budget
3) Policy: if followup_hint likely_short and client supports streaming -> convert to streaming short-chunk path and pre-warm model; else soft-backoff: return 202 queued with estimated wait; if tenant SLA is low -> degrade to fallback_model and tag response provenance.

Observability / tracing
----
- Emit x-scheduler-lane, x-scheduler-decision (serve|queue|fallback|reject), x-estimated-wait-ms
- Span annotations: scheduler.enqueue_ms, scheduler.dequeue_ms, scheduler.decision_reason

Edge cases and unresolved questions
----
- How to avoid priority inversion (many background requests with high token counts blocking interactive)? Use token-budget accounting per-lane.
- What if clients lie about priority? Need server-side heuristics and rate limits per lane.
- Prefetch cold-start cost: prefetching wastes kernel cycles; need threshold for followup probability before pre-warm.
- Interaction with Dedicated mode: tenant override must be authoritative on dedicated deployments.

Experiments to run
----
- Simulated spike test: 95th/99th latency with and without soft-backoff for interactive lane.
- Prefetch gating: measure wasted cycles vs reduction in cold-cache latency for followup flows.
- False-priority injection: abuse scenarios where clients mark everything interactive; measure SLA impact and identify mitigations.

Action items / TODO (personal)
----
- [ ] Build small prototype as middleware in ingress (Go): inspect metadata, implement simple queue, metric hook
- [ ] Add opt-in SDK flag: enable_socratic_hints=true with automatic probing
- [ ] Write benchmark harness (k6 + model emulator) for priority inversion tests
- [ ] Sync with infra on fallback models and how to surface in Console

References / links (notes)
----
- Related ticket: ENG-4521 (scheduler prototype spike)
- Prior doc: small queueing notes in confluence link above

Random scribbles (scratchpad)
----
- Maybe use token-cost accounting per tenant: each tenant has a token_budget_per_second; scheduler honors it across lanes.
- Could add client-side pacing: SDK receives 202 with Retry-After and can surface spinner with estimated wait.

End of notebook.
